name: @snopek-games/godai-mcp

tools.name: list_open_projects
tools.description: Lists the projects currently open in each Godot editor instance

tools.name: get_mcp_configuration
tools.description:
Gets the Godai MCP configuration which can be changed at runtime.

This doesn't include all configuration that can be set via command-line arguments, but only those values that can be updated at runtime.
Use the `set_mcp_configuration` tool to change these configuration values.

tools.name: set_mcp_configuration
tools.description:
Sets the Godai MCP configuration which can be changed at runtime.

This doesn't include all configuration that can be set via command-line arguments, but only those values that can be updated at runtime.
Use the `get_mcp_configuration` tool to see the current configuration values.

godot_path.description: The full path to the Godot 4 executable on your system

project_path.description: The base path where your Godot projects usually live

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description:
Lists Godot projects that are available to open

When using --global this includes those registered in the project manager and under the project base path.
Otherwise, this recursively searches in the allowed root paths.

tools.name: open_godot_project
tools.description: Opens a Godot project in a new Godot editor instance, if it isn't already open

headless.description: Launch the editor without visual or audio output (default: false). This won't have an effect if the editor is already open for this project.

tools.name: connect_signal
tools.description:
Connects a signal on one node to a method on another node, in the current scene. The connection is persistent (saved with the scene).

Both nodes must be in the current scene. The signal must exist on the 'from' node, and the method on the 'to' node.
This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

from_node.description: Path to the node emitting the signal, relative to the scene root

method.description: Name of the method to call on the receiving node

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

signal.description: Name of the signal to connect

to_node.description: Path to the node receiving the signal, relative to the scene root

tools.name: write_script
tools.description:
Replaces the entire contents of an existing script file.

You must read the script with read_script first: this fails if the script has changed since you last read it (or created/wrote it), so you don't overwrite edits you haven't seen. If it fails for that reason, read the script again and reapply your change.
If the script is open in the editor, its editor buffer is updated instead of the file on disk (so unsaved edits aren't silently clobbered); 'saved' will be false, and you can call save_script to write it to disk. If it isn't open, the file is written directly and 'saved' is true.
Use create_script to make a new script.

content.description: The full new contents of the script

file_path.description: Path to the .gd file, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: add_node
tools.description:
Creates a new node in the current scene, with the given properties set.

Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties take the raw string, with NO extra quotes (e.g. "name": "MyNode")
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`, `NodePath("../Other")`
 - To reference a saved resource: `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - To create an embedded resource: `Object(ClassName, "prop": value, ...)`, e.g. `Object(SphereMesh,"radius":2.0)`. Do NOT use SubResource() or ExtResource() - those only work inside .tscn files.
If any property name or value is invalid, an error is returned and the node is NOT created.
Otherwise, returns true and the path of the new node.
Note: Just because this returns successfully, doesn't mean all properties were able to be set to the requested value. Always check that the properties have the correct value afterwards.

node_type.description: The name of the node class to create

parent_path.description: Path to the parent node, relative the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

additionalProperties.description: The property value as a string, in Godot variant syntax (see the tool description)

properties.description: Keys are the Godot property names to set

tools.name: remove_node
tools.description: Removes the given node (and all its children) from the current scene

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_resource_properties
tools.description:
Gets the values of properties on a saved resource file (e.g. a .tres file).

If 'properties' is omitted, returns an object that maps all of the resource's property names to values.
If 'properties' is given, returns an object with a key for each requested property.
Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties are returned raw, without quotes
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`
 - A property referencing another saved resource is returned as `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - A property holding an embedded resource is summarized as `Object(ClassName)`, e.g. `Object(FastNoiseLite)`
Requested properties may use colon-separated sub-paths to address properties nested inside embedded resources or other properties, e.g. `noise:frequency` or `albedo_color:r`.
If a requested property holds an embedded resource (e.g. `noise`), all of that resource's properties are returned for it, instead of just a summary.
If a requested property can't be resolved, its value will be an object with an `error` key.

file_path.description: Path to the resource file, relative to the project root

modified_only.description: If true, only return properties that differ from their default value. Recommended when getting all properties, to keep the result small.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

properties.description: The properties to get. If omitted, all of the resource's properties are returned.

items.description: The name of a property to get (colon-separated sub-paths allowed, e.g. `albedo_color:r`)

tools.name: remove_from_group
tools.description:
Removes a node in the current scene from one or more groups.

This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

groups.description: The groups to remove the node from

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: detach_script
tools.description: Removes the script attached to a node in the current scene. This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: run_project
tools.description:
Runs the project from the editor.

'scene' controls what runs: omit it or use 'main' to run the project's main scene, 'current' to run the scene open in the editor, or a path to run a specific scene file.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

scene.description: What to run: 'main' (default), 'current', or a path to a scene file

tools.name: get_log_messages
tools.description:
Gets recent log output from the editor (print() output, warnings, and errors) captured since the editor started.

Returns a 'messages' array of the most recent log lines (oldest first).
Note: Only includes messages from code run in the editor, not from running the project.

count.description: Maximum number of recent messages to return (default 100). Use 0 for all retained messages.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_current_scene
tools.description:
Gets information about the scene that is currently opened in the Godot editor.

Returns:
 - scene_path: The path to the scene file
 - root_node_type: The class of the root Node of the scene
 - root_node_name: The name of the root Node of the scene
If no scene is currently open, it'll return an empty string for all of the above.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: open_resource
tools.description: Opens a resource in the inspector.

file_path.description: Path to the .tres file to open, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: create_script
tools.description:
Creates a new GDScript file. Does NOT open or attach it.

If 'content' is given, it is used as the file's contents. Otherwise, a minimal script extending 'base_class' is generated.

base_class.description: Base class for the generated script when 'content' is omitted (default: Node)

content.description: Full contents of the script file. If omitted, a minimal template is generated.

file_path.description: Path to the .gd file to create, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: read_script
tools.description:
Reads the contents of a script file.

If the script is currently open in the editor, its live (possibly unsaved) buffer is returned and 'open_in_editor' is true. Otherwise the contents are read from disk.
Returns 'content' and 'open_in_editor'.

file_path.description: Path to the .gd file, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: reimport
tools.description:
Reimports one or more asset files (e.g. after changing the source file or its import settings).

Each path must be an imported asset (i.e. have a .import file). If any path is invalid, nothing is reimported.

items.description: Path to an imported asset, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_import_settings
tools.description:
Gets the import settings for an imported asset (e.g. a texture or audio file).

Returns 'importer' (the name of the importer used) and 'options' (a map of import option names to values, in Godot variant syntax).

file_path.description: Path to the imported asset, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_editor_settings
tools.description:
Gets settings from the Godot editor itself (the values stored in the global editor configuration, e.g. 'interface/editor/code_font_size' or 'text_editor/appearance/whitespace/draw_tabs'). These are editor-wide preferences, not project settings.

Pass 'names' to get specific settings by name (returned regardless of whether they match their default).
Otherwise, all settings are returned, but only those whose value differs from the default; pass 'include_defaults' as true to also include settings left at their default value.

Returns 'settings': a map of setting name to value, in Godot variant syntax.

include_defaults.description: When getting all settings, also include those left at their default value (default: false)

names.description: Optional: specific setting names to get. If omitted, all settings are returned.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: create_scene
tools.description: Creates a new scene and opens it in the editor

file_path.description: Path to the .tscn file to create, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

root_node_type.description: The node type of the scene's root node

tools.name: create_resource
tools.description:
Creates a new resource. Does NOT open it automatically.

Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties take the raw string, with NO extra quotes (e.g. "resource_name": "My Resource")
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`
 - To reference a saved resource: `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - To create an embedded resource: `Object(ClassName, "prop": value, ...)`, e.g. `Object(SphereMesh,"radius":2.0)`. Do NOT use SubResource() or ExtResource() - those only work inside .tscn files.
If any property name or value is invalid, an error is returned and the resource is NOT created.

file_path.description: Path to the .tres file to create, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

additionalProperties.description: The property value as a string, in Godot variant syntax (see the tool description)

properties.description: Keys are the Godot property names to set

tools.name: get_node_groups
tools.description:
Gets the groups that nodes in the current scene belong to.

Returns an object with a key for each requested node path, containing an array of group names. Internal engine groups are omitted. If a node isn't found, its value is an empty array.

items.description: Path to a node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_project_settings
tools.description:
Gets settings from the project (the values stored in 'project.godot', e.g. 'application/config/name' or 'display/window/size/viewport_width').

Pass 'names' to get specific settings by name (returned regardless of whether they match their default).
Otherwise, all settings are returned, but only those whose value differs from the default; pass 'include_defaults' as true to also include settings left at their default value.

Returns 'settings': a map of setting name to value, in Godot variant syntax.

include_defaults.description: When getting all settings, also include those left at their default value (default: false)

names.description: Optional: specific setting names to get. If omitted, all settings are returned.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: get_current_scene_tree
tools.description:
Gets the tree for the scene that is currently opened in the Godot editor.

Returns a tree of objects representing the nodes in the scene with the following keys
 - name: The Node name
 - type: The class of the Node
 - path: The path of the node within the scene, relative to the scene root
 - script: The path to the script file, if this node has a script attached; otherwise, it'll be omitted
 - children: An array of objects with the same structure, representing the child nodes; will be omitted if node has no children
If no scene is currently open, it'll return an empty object.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: open_scene
tools.description: Opens a scene in the editor

file_path.description: Path to the .tscn file to open, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: set_node_properties
tools.description:
Sets the values of properties on specific nodes in the current scene.

Only pass in the properties you actually wish to change.
EXAMPLE: {"action": "Move node", "nodes": [{"node_path": "path/to/node", "properties": {"position": "Vector2(1, 2)"}}]}
Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties take the raw string, with NO extra quotes (e.g. "text": "Hello")
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`, `NodePath("../Other")`
 - To reference a saved resource: `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - To create an embedded resource: `Object(ClassName, "prop": value, ...)`, e.g. `Object(SphereMesh,"radius":2.0)`. Do NOT use SubResource() or ExtResource() - those only work inside .tscn files.
Property names may use colon-separated sub-paths to set properties nested inside resources or other properties, e.g. `mesh:radius`, `material:albedo_color`, `position:x`.
Note: changing a sub-property of a saved resource (`Resource("res://...")`) affects every scene using that resource.
This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system to set the properties, so as many set operations as possible should be done in a single call, so they can all be undone at once.
If any property name or value is invalid, an error is returned and NO properties are changed.
Otherwise, returns an object with a key for each node path, containing true if we were able to find the node; otherwise, false.
Note: Just because this returns successfully, doesn't mean all properties were able to be set to the requested value. Always check that the properties have the correct value afterwards.

action.description: Human-readable description of the action that will be shown in Godot's undo/redo history

node_path.description: The path to the node within the scene, relative to the scene root. May include a colon-separated property path (e.g. `MyMesh:mesh`) to address a resource or other sub-object.

additionalProperties.description: The property value as a string, in Godot variant syntax (see the tool description)

properties.description: Keys are the Godot property names to set (colon-separated sub-paths allowed, e.g. `mesh:radius`)

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: close_editor
tools.description:
Closes the Godot editor for the project.

The editor first prompts the user to save their work, and only closes once they confirm.

By default, unsaved changes are saved before closing; pass 'skip_save' as true to discard them instead.
If the user declines the prompt, the editor is not closed and this returns an error.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

skip_save.description: Discard unsaved changes instead of saving them before closing (default: false)

tools.name: set_resource_properties
tools.description:
Sets the values of properties on a saved resource file (.tres or .res), and saves the changes to the file.

Only pass in the properties you actually wish to change.
EXAMPLE: {"action": "Change color", "file_path": "res://thing.tres", "properties": {"albedo_color": "Color(1, 0, 0, 1)"}}
Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties take the raw string, with NO extra quotes (e.g. "resource_name": "My Resource")
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`
 - To reference another saved resource: `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - To create an embedded resource: `Object(ClassName, "prop": value, ...)`, e.g. `Object(FastNoiseLite,"frequency":0.1)`. Do NOT use SubResource() or ExtResource() - those only work inside .tscn files.
Property names may use colon-separated sub-paths to set properties nested inside embedded resources or other properties, e.g. `noise:frequency`, `albedo_color:r`.
Note: the changes are saved to the file immediately, and affect every scene using the resource.
This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system to set the properties, so as many set operations as possible should be done in a single call, so they can all be undone at once (undo also re-saves the file).
If any property name or value is invalid, an error is returned and NO properties are changed.
Note: Just because this returns successfully, doesn't mean all properties were able to be set to the requested value. Always check that the properties have the correct value afterwards.

action.description: Human-readable description of the action that will be shown in Godot's undo/redo history

file_path.description: Path to the .tres or .res file, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

additionalProperties.description: The property value as a string, in Godot variant syntax (see the tool description)

properties.description: Keys are the Godot property names to set (colon-separated sub-paths allowed, e.g. `albedo_color:r`)

tools.name: instantiate_scene
tools.description:
Instantiates a saved scene (.tscn/.scn) as a child node in the current scene, like adding an instanced scene in the editor.

Returns true and the path of the new instance node.
This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

name.description: Optional name for the new instance node

parent_path.description: Path to the parent node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

scene_path.description: Path to the scene file to instantiate, relative to the project root

tools.name: save_script
tools.description:
Saves a script's unsaved changes from the editor to its file.

If the script is open in the editor, its current (possibly unsaved) contents are written to disk. If it isn't open, there is nothing to save and this is a no-op.

file_path.description: Path to the .gd file, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: stop_project
tools.description: Stops the running project, if any.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: set_import_settings
tools.description:
Changes the import settings for an imported asset, and reimports it.

Only pass the options you wish to change. Option values are strings in Godot variant syntax (e.g. `2`, `true`, `2.0`); a value that isn't valid variant syntax is taken as a raw string.
Use get_import_settings to see the available option names and the current importer.

file_path.description: Path to the imported asset, relative to the project root

importer.description: Optional: change the importer used for this asset

additionalProperties.description: The option value, as a string in Godot variant syntax

options.description: Import options to set (keys are option names)

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: execute_editor_script
tools.description:
Executes the given GDScript code in the editor, in the context of a Node that is a child of the scene currently being edited.

For modifying the current scene, use the other tools when possible.
However, if you do use a script to modify the current scene, you MUST use `EditorUndoRedoManager` from `EditorInterface.get_editor_undo_redo()`, and the action name MUST end with "(AI)".
You can find nodes relative to the scene root using `EditorInterface.get_edited_scene_root().get_node_or_null(node_path)`.
Two helper methods have been provided:
 - `func editor_undo_redo_create_node(p_undo_redo: EditorUndoRedoManager, p_parent: Node, p_child: Node) -> void`
 - `func editor_undo_redo_remove_node(p_undo_redo: EditorUndoRedoManager, p_parent: Node, p_child: Node) -> void`
If you are using `EditorUndoRedoManager` to add or remove a node, you MUST call one of those helper methods before calling `commit_action()`. This will add some `add_do_method()` and `add_undo_method()` calls to ensure the changes are synchronized to the live game if the game is running.
If the script successfully runs, the output from `print()` will be returned.

code.description: A snippet of GDScript code. It should use tabs rather than spaces for indentation. Don't wrap the code in a `_ready()` function.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: restart_editor
tools.description:
Restarts the Godot editor for the project.

The editor first prompts the user to save their work, and only restarts once they confirm.

By default, unsaved changes are saved before restarting; pass 'skip_save' as true to discard them instead.
If the user declines the prompt, the editor is not restarted and this returns an error.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

skip_save.description: Discard unsaved changes instead of saving them before restarting (default: false)

tools.name: set_editor_settings
tools.description:
Changes settings in the Godot editor itself (editor-wide preferences, not project settings). Changes take effect immediately and are persisted by the editor.

Pass 'settings': a map of setting name (e.g. 'interface/editor/code_font_size') to value. Values are strings in Godot variant syntax (e.g. `16`, `true`, `2.0`); a value that isn't valid variant syntax is taken as a raw string.
Use get_editor_settings to see the available setting names and their current values.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

additionalProperties.description: The setting value, as a string in Godot variant syntax

settings.description: Settings to set (keys are setting names)

tools.name: get_node_properties
tools.description:
Gets the values of properties on specific nodes in the current scene.

Returns an object with a key for each requested node path, containing an object that maps property names to values.
Property values are strings in Godot variant syntax:
 - String properties are returned raw, without quotes
 - Other types use Godot syntax, e.g. `0.5`, `true`, `Vector2(1, 2)`, `Color(1, 0, 0, 1)`
 - A property referencing a saved resource is returned as `Resource("res://path/to/file.tres")`
 - A property holding an embedded resource is summarized as `Object(ClassName)`, e.g. `Object(SphereMesh)`
To inspect the properties of an embedded resource, append a colon-separated property path to the node path: `MyMesh:mesh` returns the properties of the mesh resource, and `MyMesh:mesh:radius` returns just that value.
If a node isn't found, its value will be an empty object. If a property path can't be resolved, its value will be an object with an `error` key.

modified_only.description: If true, only return properties that differ from their default value. Recommended, to keep the result small.

items.description: The path to the node within the scene, relative to the scene root. May include a colon-separated property path (e.g. `MyMesh:mesh`) to inspect a resource or other sub-object.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: save_scene
tools.description: Saves the scene currently open in the editor to its file. Fails if no scene is open, or if the current scene has never been saved (has no file path).

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: disconnect_signal
tools.description:
Disconnects a previously-connected signal between two nodes in the current scene.

This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

from_node.description: Path to the node emitting the signal, relative to the scene root

method.description: Name of the connected method on the receiving node

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

signal.description: Name of the signal to disconnect

to_node.description: Path to the node receiving the signal, relative to the scene root

tools.name: open_script
tools.description: Opens a script file in the editor's script editor.

file_path.description: Path to the .gd file to open, relative to the project root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: attach_script
tools.description:
Attaches an existing script file to a node in the current scene.

The script's base type must be compatible with the node's type. Use create_script first if the script doesn't exist yet.
This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

script_path.description: Path to the script file, relative to the project root

tools.name: set_project_settings
tools.description:
Changes settings in the project and saves 'project.godot'.

Pass 'settings': a map of setting name (e.g. 'display/window/size/viewport_width') to value. Values are strings in Godot variant syntax (e.g. `1280`, `true`, `2.0`); a value that isn't valid variant syntax is taken as a raw string.
Settings that don't exist yet are created. Use get_project_settings to see the available setting names and their current values.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

additionalProperties.description: The setting value, as a string in Godot variant syntax

settings.description: Settings to set (keys are setting names)

tools.name: get_selected_nodes
tools.description:
Gets the nodes currently selected in the editor for the current scene.

Returns an object with a 'node_paths' key: an array of node paths (relative to the scene root) for the selected nodes.
If no scene is open or nothing is selected, 'node_paths' is an empty array.

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

tools.name: add_to_group
tools.description:
Adds a node in the current scene to one or more groups, persistently (so they're saved with the scene).

This uses the Godot editor's undo/redo system.

groups.description: The groups to add the node to

node_path.description: Path to the node, relative to the scene root

project_path.description: The path to the Godot project. It must already be open in the Godot editor.

instructions:
Open and control the Godot editor: inspect and edit the scene tree, node properties, scripts, resources, and project settings. Prefer these tools over editing .tscn/.tres/.gd files on disk - the editor owns that state and direct file edits can be clobbered or rejected.

Most tools require a project_path; call list_open_projects (or open_godot_project) first.
